questions.stem: While interpreting a graph of meaning, which statement best captures reference?

options.text: Words point to things and situations in the world

questions.explanation: Reference points to things and situations in the world. Mental, spelling, and sound-only views are too narrow.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Language: What a Speaker Means Beyond What Is Said
questions.stem: While interpreting a graph of utterances, a claim says implicature is identical to entailment; is this right?

options.text: Yes, because both are logical consequences
No, because implicature is inferred, not strict

questions.explanation: Implicature is inferred and cancellable, not a strict entailment. Pronunciation is irrelevant.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Language: The Part of an Utterance a Speaker Does Not Say Out Loud
questions.stem: While interpreting a graph of utterances, which statement best captures ellipsis?
questions.explanation: Ellipsis omits surface words that context recovers. It is grammatical and does not remove meaning or add words.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Language: The Sounds a Speaker Makes That Are Not Words
questions.stem: While interpreting a graph of speech, a claim says paralanguage is just noise; is this right?

options.text: No, because paralinguistic cues carry meaningful information

questions.explanation: Paralinguistic cues carry meaningful information. Denying them or reducing them to noise or spelling is wrong.
